claim: For every integer \(q\ge 2\), let \(P_q\) be the finite \(T_0\)-space with two minimal points \(a,b\), \(q\) maximal points \(c_1,\ldots,c_q\), and all relations \(a,b<c_i\). Then the unbased self-homotopy set has exactly \(1+2(q^q-q)\) classes. One class consists of all self-maps inducing zero on \(H_1(P_q;\mathbb Z)\) and has exactly \(2(q+1)^q+7q\) maps. Every other class is a singleton: these are exactly the maps that permute \(a,b\) and send the maximal level nonconstantly into itself, equivalently exactly the self-maps inducing a nonzero endomorphism of \(H_1(P_q;\mathbb Z)\). Thus every homologically nontrivial self-map is an isolated point of the finite function space \(P_q^{P_q}\). The total number of continuous self-maps is \(2(q+1)^q+2q^q+5q\).

integrity.claim_scope: exact unbased self-homotopy component structure and counts for every complete height-two finite space P_q with two minima and q maxima
integrity.novelty_boundary: finite-space/poset correspondence, bouquet weak homotopy type, and general homotopy machinery are prior work; the all-q component formula and equivalence between isolated self-maps and nonzero integral H1 action are the claimed new content
integrity.proof_core: finite-space fence homotopy plus an exhaustive case split on the images of the two minima, a direct isolation argument, and a graph-cycle witness for nonzero H1 action

scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to the complete height-two family with two minimal points and q maximal points.
Distinct isolated self-maps can induce the same first-homology endomorphism; the theorem identifies zero versus nonzero action, not a complete homological invariant of singleton classes.
The literature search is targeted and leaves residual risk from obscure or unindexed historical sources.
title: Exact self-homotopy classes of complete height-two finite bouquet models
